paper.title: Solution of the Transcendental Equation w e^w = x (Algorithm 443)
authors: W. P. Gowley (as listed in the frame; probably Crowley, not verified)
paper.venue: Communications of the ACM 16(2), 123-124, February 1973 (the frame lists it as TOMS 16,2; the archive header says CACM VOL. 16, NO. 2)
paper.url: not fetched by scout; the paper text was not read

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 443.gz (a shell archive, read but not run: Fortran/Sp/Drivers/driver.f, Makefile and res; Fortran/Sp/Src/src.f)
code.archive: sha256 bf664e74f2700a5c8a2f6c27b4cbc9e1d7b37c19a792764fd73c6941f642026f (downloaded by scout 2026-11-27 from netlib.org/toms/443.gz, the single .gz file)
code.note: The archive is a /bin/sh shell archive that creates Fortran/ files. The rerun must unpack it into its own directory and not run it as a script; the driver calls WEW_A, the Lambert W routine in src.f. The shipped res file is the expected output of the driver, from TEST01 (Test WEW_A).

claim.location: Shipped reference output, Fortran/Sp/Drivers/res, block 'TEST01 / Test WEW_A to evaluate Lambert's W function', row x = 1.0000: 'Exact Value 0.5671', 'Computed 0.56714326'. The driver calls WEW_A(x) for x = 0.0, 0.5, ..., and the Computed column is the code's own output.

reference.file: Fortran/Sp/Drivers/res (embedded in 443.gz, lines 308-363 of the decompressed shell archive)
reference.sha256: b0ad6d705c4ca2ca094039f176486720d0a39a5d732185f789ae4b9a628da4e1 (sha256 of the decompressed shell-archive text, read by scout; the .gz itself is bf664e74...)

claim.paper_value: W(1.0) computed by WEW_A = 0.56714326 (printed to 8 decimals in res; the exact W(1) = 0.5671432904...)
claim.metric: value returned by WEW_A at x = 1.0 (the Computed column, TEST01), compared as a number
claim.determinism: deterministic (no random input; the test points are fixed in driver.f)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The reference is printed to 8 decimals, so the rounding step is 5e-9. The printed value differs from the exact W(1) by 3e-8, which is the original code's own error, so a tolerance tighter than 1e-7 would test rounding of the print, not the routine. A value outside 1e-7 would be a real change in WEW_A's output. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: a few evaluations of a closed-form-style iteration.
cost.data_size: None: the driver generates its own inputs.
cost.data_licence: No data. Code licence is not stated in the archive; the rerun should record it.

why: The authors' shipped driver prints a computed Lambert W value for the transcendental equation w e^w = x; the number needs the iterative routine to evaluate, and the value tests the old Fortran on a modern compiler rather than a closed form, since W(1) has no elementary form.
